Hi all — I ran Orison's preliminary numbers against our sizing model (attached PDF). Key assumptions I used are inline below. If any change, ping me and I will rerun.

Assumptions:
- Median prompt: 320 tokens, median response: 180 tokens
- Average tokens/sec per GPU (mixed quantized profile): 600 tokens/sec (sustained for generation workloads)
- Target P95 latency SLO: 300ms per request (interactive mode)
- Peak concurrency target for ramp: 120 

Sizing options (rounded):
- Minimum (cost‑conservative): 8 x A40‑class equivalents — supports baseline throughput with limited headroom (expected token capacity ~2.9M tokens/min)
- Target (recommended): 12 x A40‑class equivalents — comfortable headroom for spikes and KV cache effectiveness
- Buffer (high‑availability): 16 x A40‑class equivalents — for multi‑region fallback and burst pools

Lead time implications: reservation commit for Dedicated pool (12 units range) -> allocate inventory in 8–10 weeks; if Orison needs private VPC in a specific cloud region we control, factor in 1–2 week network/infra prep; on‑prem longer for procurement and rack readiness.

I attached a one‑page capacity playbook with a checklist we use during procurement: network preflight, KMS access, SOC2 evidence collection, test token budget, and performance soak windows.

I'll bring these numbers to the scoping call.

—Marcus

Elaine — quick reply to address your three questions and propose next steps before the scoping call: 

1) KV cache: we model cache hit rate conservatively at 20–40% for mixed interactive workloads during sizing. For Orison's many short follow‑on prompts, assume the lower end initially; if your bench shows higher reuse we recalculate and typically drop required units by ~10–25%. We will include cache sensitivity runs in the bench.

2) Vertical scaling / variant swaps: for Dedicated pools we prequalify quantized variants on our staging infra; swapping to a compatible quantized model variant typically requires no additional physical lead time if the GPU type and capacity remain the same — it's a software-side rollout and can often be done within the rollout window. If you require different hardware (e.g., higher memory GPUs), that does affect procurement/lead time.

3) SOC2 and infra artifacts: we'll share a redacted SOC2 summary, network diagram checklist, and an evidence matrix (what we can provide vs what we expect from you). I'll put those artifacts in the Drive folder and share with your legal/security.

Procurement / commitment schedule (high level):
- Week 0: Sign MAP (evaluation kick) and bench scoping call
- Week 1–3: Bench runs, perf & quality validation, security Q&A
- Week 3–4: Finalize sizing & pricing, legal review of reservation T&Cs
- Week 4–6: PO issuance and payment terms alignment
- Week 6–10: Hardware allocation and Dedicated pool provisioning (target start of capacity delivery)

If that high‑level schedule looks OK, Marcus and I will convert this into the MAP milestones and a short commitment schedule for legal review. I'll also attach the sample reservation T&Cs.

Thanks — will see you on the scoping call tomorrow.
